# OBS014 `goto-end-do`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A `go to` jumps to the `end do` of a loop.

## Why

Jumping to the labelled `end do` of a loop is the pre-Fortran 90 way of starting the next
iteration. `cycle` says the same thing without a label, and keeps working when the loop is moved
or renamed.

## Reported

```fortran
do i = 1, n
  if (skip(i)) go to 10
  a(i) = 0.0
10 end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
do i = 1, n
  if (skip(i)) cycle
  a(i) = 0.0
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS014] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS014` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB094` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
